candidate.title: 4sUDRB-seq
candidate.scope: Assigned 4sUDRB-seq middle row of the supplied Illumina poster crop: a single retained route from cellular DRB inhibition and release through 4sU labeling, biotin–streptavidin enrichment, elution and cDNA preparation. The card title, matching catalogue heading and Fuchs 2014 paper establish this target. Independent neighboring BruDRB-seq and PRO-seq rows, cropped top-margin labels and the isolated EDTA structure are contextual; no arrows or alternative marker connect them to the assigned row. Primary-paper detail is qualified to the 2014 implementation and clarifies interfaces without expanding the broad library-preparation block.

operations.label: Reverse transcription amplification
operations.description: Convert enriched RNA into cDNA and amplify through the broadly depicted library-preparation block. The supported 2014 interface omits poly(A) selection.
operations.information_effect: cDNA-derived sequence reads represent the genomic distribution of enriched newly synthesized RNA. Comparison of the advancing transcription wave across post-release samples supports gene-specific elongation-rate inference; a single cDNA endpoint does not itself encode a rate. The 2014 paper describes relative initiation-frequency inference, while the supplied 2015 protocol abstract distinguishes elongation speed from the rate of Pol II transition into active elongation. These source-specific quantities are not asserted to be interchangeable. The inspected 2014 library lacks strand specificity; residual mature RNA and incomplete DRB arrest limit specificity.
